introH2: 🛂 What kinds of hotels are there in Aranyaprathet, and how do you pick the right one for your trip?
introHtml: Aranyaprathet is a town on the far edge of the Thai-Cambodian border, and most people come here with a clear goal — crossing at the Khlong Luek checkpoint to Poipet and Siem Reap, shopping at Rong Kluea Market, or bringing the family for a getaway · That makes choosing a place to stay here different from a typical tourist town, because what matters most is location and function rather than a pretty view or luxury · There's more variety here than you'd expect — a bike-themed hotel with a BMX Pump Track and its own saltwater pool, a boutique hotel with roomy rooms and a swimming pool, a small garden resort with the warm service of staying at a relative's house, all the way down to bungalows and budget hotels in the low hundreds of baht that are a short walk from the border · A lot of people book the wrong type of stay for their trip — say, planning an early-morning crossing but ending up far from the border, or wanting the kids to swim but picking a place with no pool · This article rounds up 10 hotels in Aranyaprathet that we've reviewed in depth, each one based on reading real guest reviews on booking platforms, with the good points and the honest caveats, prices compared across 3 sites, and direct booking links for all of them
mrtHtml: Aranyaprathet has no rail system and limited public transport, so the easiest way to get around is driving yourself, or taking a train/bus and having your hotel arrange transfers, since Grab is scarce in the area · The town's main landmarks: Khlong Luek checkpoint — the crossing point to Poipet on the Cambodian side; go early in the morning when it's less crowded and cooler · Rong Kluea Market — the largest border market in Thailand, with secondhand goods and a wide range of products · Aranyaprathet train station + bus terminal — in the town center, near several budget stays · The hotels in this set are spread across the town center, right by Rong Kluea Market, and in quiet suburban zones, so before you book, check the distance to the border and the market against your travel plans

entries.name: The Velo's Hotel and Pumptrack
entries.revCount: Trip.com 8.4 · Among the top-rated in Aranyaprathet on Tripadvisor
entries.badge: 🚲 The most one-of-a-kind · Has a Pump Track
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Aranyaprathet · about 15 min to Rong Kluea Market and the border
entries.addr: 65 Thanawithi Road, Aranyaprathet Subdistrict, Aranyaprathet District, Sa Kaeo
entries.storyHtml: If there's one place in Aranyaprathet that gets reviewers saying "I never thought a border town would have a hotel like this," it's this one — The Velo's Hotel and Pumptrack is Thailand's first bike-themed hotel, built around a single idea, "cycling," until it became a 90-room, 4-star boutique with in-house features nothing else in the area can match · The real star is the BMX Pump Track, more than 400 meters long, designed in collaboration with Claudio Caluori, the world-famous mountain-bike champion — a continuous rolling asphalt track, open to use for free, that takes bikes, skateboards, and rollerblades, with lights for riding until around 10pm · Paired with a semi-Olympic saltwater pool with a slide that reviewers agree has clear, non-stinging water where kids can play all day and not want to leave, plus a separate kids' pool so parents can relax · There are 4 room types, from Superior up to Deluxe Pool Access, which steps straight into the pool from the balcony, and a Bike Type with in-room bike storage for cyclists · Real reviews from Trip.com, Booking.com, Agoda, and Tripadvisor agree the rooms are clean, spacious, modern in design, and well soundproofed · An honest caveat from the reviews: breakfast is the most-criticized point, with few options that run out fast — go down around 7:00–8:00am for a fuller spread · The building is 3 stories with no elevator, so if you're with elderly travelers or heavy luggage, ask for a ground-floor room · Some of the loaner bikes are in rough shape, so check the brakes and tires before letting kids ride, and front-desk service can occasionally be less than cheerful · This is a stay that sells experience and fun, best suited to families bringing kids to swim, cyclists who want a training track on-site, and anyone who wants a clean, modern room for a night before crossing into Poipet
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're with kids and swimming is the main plan, a Deluxe Pool Access room that steps into the pool from the balcony is very much worth the convenience · Try the Pump Track in the morning or evening when the sun isn't harsh, and plan around breakfast by going down early or picking up something to eat in town as backup
pros: 400-meter BMX Pump Track, free to use, nothing else in the area can match it
Semi-Olympic saltwater pool with a slide, clear water, kids love it
Clean, spacious, modern-design rooms, well soundproofed (per reviews)
Location in Aranyaprathet town, near the market and bus terminal, free parking
cons: Breakfast has few options and runs out fast — the most-criticized point
3-story building with no elevator · some loaner bikes are in poor shape
Front-desk service can occasionally be less than cheerful (per reviews)

entries.name: OB-Oon Resort
entries.badge: 💛 Warm service that lives up to its name
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Soi Kilo 3, Fak Huai · about 10–15 min to the border
entries.addr: 99 Soi Kilo 3, Fak Huai Subdistrict, Aranyaprathet District, Sa Kaeo
entries.storyHtml: OB-Oon Resort, whose Thai name "Ob-Oon" means warm, really does live up to it — a small resort of about 6 rooms in a garden setting in Aranyaprathet, built around cleanliness, quiet, and friendly service · The thing real reviews agree on most is the staff service, which scored full marks for Service on TripAdvisor, with words that come up again and again being "friendly," "helpful," and "warm," matching the resort's name exactly · Several staff are praised for giving good advice on crossing at the Khlong Luek checkpoint, getting to Rong Kluea Market, and arranging rides, which is valuable for first-timers in the area · Rooms come in several types — Double, Twin, Triple, Family, and Holiday Home, a small private cottage — all with air conditioning, a fridge, a flat-screen TV, and bathroom amenities · Some rooms have a small balcony looking out over the garden, a spot many guests like for morning coffee · An advantage worth noting is the on-site restaurant, which helps a lot in an area where outside eateries are far off, especially for breakfast or a late meal after returning from the border, plus a 24-hour front desk and free parking · An honest caveat from the reviews: the Soi Kilo 3 location is fairly quiet, with restaurants and convenience stores some distance away, so if you don't have a car, ask the front desk to arrange transport in advance · Online reviews are still limited given the size of the place, some facility details such as a swimming pool don't match across all sources so check first, and some channels note cash-only payment, so bring enough cash · Best suited to Rong Kluea Market shoppers, Poipet border crossers, and families who want a small, quiet garden resort at an easy price
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Bring enough cash, since some channels are cash-only · If you don't have your own car, ask the front desk to arrange a ride from the Aranyaprathet train station or bus terminal, and if you'll eat late or before dawn, check the kitchen hours ahead of time
pros: Warm, friendly service, full marks for Service on TripAdvisor
Clean rooms, comfortable beds, a quiet, private garden setting
On-site restaurant, 24-hour front desk, free parking
Starting around ฿880/night, good value for a stopover before crossing the border
cons: Quiet location, outside eateries are far off, you'll need a car or to arrange rides
Only about 6 rooms, fills up fast in peak season · still few online reviews
Some channels are cash-only, so bring enough cash

entries.name: Tournesol Boutique Hotel
entries.revCount: Trip.com 8.0 · Boutique with roomy rooms and a saltwater pool
entries.badge: 🏊 Boutique with a pool · good for families
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Aranyaprathet KM.5 · near Rong Kluea Market
entries.addr: 479 Suwannason Road, KM.5, Aranyaprathet Subdistrict, Aranyaprathet District, Sa Kaeo
entries.storyHtml: Tournesol Boutique Hotel is the pick for anyone who wants a stay that looks a step above the usual border hotel while still keeping to a budget — a 3.5-star boutique with about 51 rooms, decorated in a warm-toned Thai-Balinese style, in the Aranyaprathet KM.5 area near Rong Kluea Market and the Khlong Luek checkpoint · What sets it apart from the budget stays nearby is the saltwater pool with separate kids' and adults' sections, which reviewers call attractive and the spot families like most · The rooms earn praise for being spacious and clean with comfortable beds, and many have a balcony overlooking the pool or garden, feeling more like a small villa than a standard hotel room · Rooms come in several tiers, from Standard Double and Twin that often include breakfast, up to a pool-view Deluxe and a Family / Suite that sleeps several and suits families · Staff are praised as friendly and helpful with border crossings, and there's free on-site parking · An honest caveat from the reviews: breakfast and Wi-Fi are where opinions split — some say breakfast is unremarkable, with eggs sometimes arriving cold and coffee from a sachet, while Wi-Fi drops often and the signal is unsteady in some rooms · On top of that, the hotel restaurant's food is pricier than outside eateries, so if you're particular about breakfast, set your expectations or head into town for a coffee shop as backup · Overall, best suited to families with kids, couples, and border crossers who want a boutique with roomy rooms and a pool at a good price
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're with family and the kids love the water, pick a room near the pool and set aside afternoon time for them to swim · Set your expectations on breakfast and Wi-Fi, where opinions split, and if you want a proper meal, look for an eatery in Aranyaprathet town that's easier on the wallet than the hotel food
pros: Saltwater pool with separate kids' and adults' sections, a spot families like
Spacious, clean rooms, comfortable beds, balconies, Thai-Balinese atmosphere
Location near Rong Kluea Market and the Khlong Luek checkpoint, free parking
Friendly staff, helpful with border crossings
cons: Unremarkable breakfast, eggs sometimes cold and coffee from a sachet (per reviews)
Wi-Fi drops often, signal unsteady in some rooms
Hotel restaurant food is pricier than outside eateries

entries.name: La Villa Boutique Hotel
entries.revCount: Trip.com 8.4 · Small boutique with a pool + sauna
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Aranyaprathet, Ban Khok Rd · near Rong Kluea Market
entries.addr: 11/1-11/2 Ban Khok Road, Aranyaprathet Subdistrict, Aranyaprathet District, Sa Kaeo
entries.storyHtml: La Villa Boutique Hotel Aranyaprathet is a small boutique hotel of about 17 rooms that leans into privacy and quiet, in Aranyaprathet near Rong Kluea Market · What sets it apart from similarly priced boutiques nearby is that it has both a swimming pool and a Finnish sauna at a price that's still easy, which is rare in a border town, and the top room, the Suite with Garden View, even has a private jacuzzi and an in-room sauna · Real reviews agree the rooms are clean with strong showers and comfortable beds, and the European-style breakfast earns praise in many reviews · Because it's a small place with few rooms, each one gets fairly thorough attention, and the overall feel is calm and quiet, more like a private villa than a hotel · Rooms come in several tiers, from Superior, Deluxe Twin, and Cabana Garden Terrace with a garden-view balcony, up to a Suite with a jacuzzi · Staff are praised as friendly, good at arranging rides and giving border-crossing info, and there's free parking · An honest caveat from the reviews: the location is fairly quiet, with outside restaurants a long walk or short drive away, so if you don't have a car, have the front desk arrange a tuk-tuk in advance · Opinions on breakfast vary a bit — some like it, some find the options limited — and a few rooms have had reviews mentioning mosquitoes and fairly firm beds · Overall, best suited to couples and anyone who wants a small, quiet, private boutique with a pool and sauna at an easy price, before shopping at Rong Kluea Market or crossing into Poipet
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you don't have your own car, have the front desk arrange a tuk-tuk in advance, since outside eateries are a long walk · If you want the full treat, look at the Suite with Garden View, which has an in-room jacuzzi and sauna, and set your expectations on breakfast, where opinions vary
pros: Has both a swimming pool and a Finnish sauna at an easy price, rare in this area
Clean rooms, strong showers, comfortable beds, European breakfast earns praise
Small boutique, about 17 rooms, quiet and private like a villa
Friendly staff, helpful with rides and border-crossing info, free parking
cons: Quiet location, outside restaurants are a long walk or short drive away
Limited breakfast options, opinions vary a bit (per reviews)
Some rooms have had reviews mentioning mosquitoes and fairly firm beds

entries.type: 3.5-Star Hotel · In Town, Has a Pool
entries.name: Indochina Hotel Aranyaprathet
entries.revCount: Trip.com 8.9 · Highest score in this article
entries.badge: 🏆 Highest score · big pool, new rooms
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Aranyaprathet, Thanawithi Rd · near Rong Kluea Market
entries.addr: 154 Moo 6, Thanawithi Road, Ban Mai Nong Sai Subdistrict, Aranyaprathet District, Sa Kaeo
entries.storyHtml: Among the Aranyaprathet stays we've reviewed, measured on score alone, Indochina Hotel Aranyaprathet is the highest in this article at 8.9 on Trip.com — a 3.5-star hotel with about 116 rooms in the Aranyaprathet area on Thanawithi Road, near Rong Kluea Market and the Khlong Luek checkpoint · What reviews mention most is the large saltwater pool with attractive landscaping around it and the new, spacious, spotless rooms, which feel like more than you'd pay for at a border-town hotel · Another thing that sets it apart from others in the area is the breakfast that many reviews call generous and better than expected, which runs counter to many Aranyaprathet stays that tend to get criticized on the morning meal · Rooms come in several tiers, from a new, spacious 24-sq.m. Deluxe, up to a Junior Twin Suite, a Honeymoon Suite with a bathtub that suits couples, and the largest Grand Suite · Staff are praised as friendly with a warm welcome, and there's free parking · An honest caveat from the reviews: there's live music at night that plays late, fairly loud early in the evening, so if you sleep light, ask for a room facing the parking lot, which is quieter · And while it's in the Aranyaprathet area, it's a fair distance from the Khlong Luek checkpoint and Rong Kluea Market — you'll need a ride, not a walk — so allow travel time and have the front desk arrange transport, and some breakfast dishes are served fairly cold · Overall, best suited to anyone who wants a hotel with a large pool, new clean rooms, and good breakfast, at the best value in the Aranyaprathet area
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you sleep light and want quiet, ask for a room facing the parking lot, since there's live music at night · If you're set on an early border crossing or shopping at Rong Kluea Market, allow travel time and have the front desk arrange a ride in advance, since the hotel is some distance away and you'll need transport
pros: Highest score in the article at 8.9 · large saltwater pool with attractive landscaping
New, spacious, spotless rooms, more than you'd pay for at a border-town hotel
Generous breakfast, better than expected (a frequently praised point)
Friendly staff, warm welcome, free parking
cons: Live music plays late, loud early in the evening
Location is far from the Khlong Luek checkpoint and Rong Kluea Market, you'll need a ride
Some breakfast dishes are served fairly cold (per reviews)

entries.name: My Room by Sermsub
entries.revCount: Trip.com 7.9 · A stylish minimalist boutique, above its price
entries.badge: ✨ Stylish design + free transfers within a short radius
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Aranyaprathet, Thanawithi Rd · near Rong Kluea Market & train station
tags: 🚐 Free transfers within a short radius
entries.addr: 168 Moo 2, Thanawithi Road, Ban Mai Nong Sai, Aranyaprathet District, Sa Kaeo
entries.storyHtml: My Room by Sermsub is a small boutique hotel of just 18 rooms that many reviews call clean and more stylish than its price — decorated in a warm-toned minimalist style in the Aranyaprathet area, near Rong Kluea Market, the Khlong Luek checkpoint, and the train station · The main draw is rooms that look better than their star rating, starting at just around ฿800/night, which real reviews agree are clean, with cold air conditioning, comfortable beds, and stylish decor you wouldn't expect at this price in a border town · Another thing that helps travelers without a car is the free transfer service within a short radius, which matters in a town where Grab is hard to find and public transport is limited, plus a 24-hour front desk and security, and free parking · Rooms come in several tiers, from a compact Comfort Twin/Double entry room, up to a roomier, better-equipped Superior King and Deluxe King · Every room has air conditioning, a TV, a safe, a minibar, and an en-suite bathroom with hot water · An honest caveat from the reviews: there's no on-site restaurant and breakfast isn't a focus, so you'll need to plan your own meals or use the free transfer to find an eatery in town · The soi is fairly quiet, not on a street lined with shops, and finding food nearby at night isn't convenient, so if you arrive late, pick up something to eat on the way, and some decor and in-room items are starting to show their age with use · Overall, best suited to travelers passing through who care more about a clean, stylish room than full facilities, before shopping at Rong Kluea Market or crossing into Poipet
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: There's no dining room here and breakfast isn't a focus, so if you arrive late, pick up something to eat on the way, or use the free transfer within a short radius to find an eatery in town and at Rong Kluea Market · Great for travelers without a car who want a clean, stylish room on a small budget
pros: Clean rooms, stylish minimalist decor, cold air conditioning, comfortable beds, above its price
Free transfers within a short radius, a big help for those without a car
Location near Rong Kluea Market, the Khlong Luek checkpoint, and the train station
24-hour front desk and security, free parking
cons: No on-site restaurant and breakfast isn't a focus, you'll need to eat out
Quiet soi, finding food nearby at night isn't convenient
Some decor and in-room items are starting to show their age with use

entries.type: 2–3 Star Budget Hotel · On the Border
entries.name: At Border Hotel
entries.revCount: Trip.com 8.0 · The best location for the border and market
entries.badge: 🛂 Walk to the Poipet border + Rong Kluea Market
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Next to Rong Kluea Market · walk to the Poipet border
entries.addr: 654 Rong Kluea Market, Pa Rai Subdistrict, Aranyaprathet District, Sa Kaeo Province
entries.storyHtml: If location is what you care about most because you're here to cross the border or shop the market, At Border Hotel is the stay whose name says it all — a budget hotel in the 2–3 star range with about 64 rooms, sitting right next to Rong Kluea Market and a few steps from the Poipet border, which no other stay in this set comes close to matching · The clear draw is convenience taken to the limit — you can walk straight over to queue for the crossing without calling a ride, and it's under two minutes on foot to Rong Kluea Market for shopping and food · Real reviews praise the good cold air conditioning, strong Wi-Fi that actually works, and free parking, and the 24-hour front desk makes it very convenient for anyone arriving late or setting off before dawn to cross the border · Rooms come as Standard Double with a large bed and Standard Twin with two single beds, suiting couples or friends, starting at just around ฿680/night · An honest caveat that has to be said plainly from the reviews: room quality and cleanliness are inconsistent, with reviews mentioning bug problems, stained linens, and maintenance issues in some rooms, so the best move is to inspect the room at check-in and don't hesitate to ask to switch rooms if it's not okay · The market area and streets are busy from early morning, so low floors or street-facing rooms hear the noise — if you sleep light, ask for a high floor or an inner-facing room · And there's almost nothing to do around the hotel besides walking the market · Best suited to anyone needing an overnight before or after the Thai-Cambodian crossing and to Rong Kluea Market shoppers on a budget, who value location over a polished room
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Always inspect the room at check-in and don't hesitate to tell the front desk you want to switch rooms if you run into cleanliness or bug problems · If you have trouble sleeping, ask for a high floor or an inner-facing room that doesn't face the street, since the market area is busy from early morning
pros: Location next to the Poipet border, walk over to queue for the crossing in a few steps
Next to Rong Kluea Market, under two minutes on foot, handy for shopping and food
Good cold air conditioning, strong Wi-Fi that actually works, free parking
24-hour front desk, convenient for late check-in and pre-dawn check-out
cons: Cleanliness and room condition are inconsistent, some rooms have bugs or stained linens
Noise from the market area and street, especially low-floor rooms
Almost nothing to do around the hotel besides walking the market

entries.name: Station ONE Hotel
entries.revCount: Trip.com 8.4 · Walk to the Aranyaprathet bus terminal
entries.badge: 🚌 Town-center location, walk to the bus terminal
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Central Aranyaprathet · walk to the bus terminal
tags: 🚌 Walk to the Aranyaprathet bus terminal
🛍️ Near Rong Kluea Market & the border
entries.addr: 41 Thanawithi Road, Aranyaprathet District, Sa Kaeo Province
entries.storyHtml: Station ONE Hotel is a 3-star budget stay with about 40 rooms, well suited to anyone who wants a single clean night at an easy price and to walk to everything in central Aranyaprathet · The location's strength is that you can walk to the Aranyaprathet bus terminal and train station, and it's near Rong Kluea Market and the Poipet border, making it a great base for anyone arriving by bus or train who needs a bed before crossing the border or hitting the market · Real reviews praise the rooms as roomier than the price, clean to standard, and the front-desk staff as friendly and helpful with travel, which is valuable for first-timers in the area, plus there's free parking · Rooms come as Standard Twin with two single beds, suiting friends or families, and Standard King with a large bed, suiting couples or solo travelers, starting at just around ฿600/night (rates rise during long weekends or festivals when border-crossing crowds are heavy, so book ahead) · An honest caveat that has to be said plainly from the reviews: this is a building that's been open for over 20 years, so it shows its age, with some spots getting worn, and the elevator has had stretches of being out of order, requiring carrying things up the stairs, so if you have heavy luggage, ask for a low-floor room · Some bathrooms have a musty smell and towels are sometimes short, and reviews mention mosquitoes at night and fairly thin walls, so bring mosquito repellent · This is a practical, working stay, not a leisure resort, best suited to anyone who values a town-center location and value over a brand-new room
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you have heavy luggage, ask for a low-floor room right at booking, since the elevator has had problems at times · Bring mosquito repellent and set your expectations on value and the town-center location, and if you walk in, try asking to see the room before deciding
pros: Town-center location, walk to the Aranyaprathet bus terminal and train station
Near Rong Kluea Market and the Poipet border, a good base before crossing
Rooms roomier than the price, clean to standard
Friendly front-desk staff, helpful with travel, free parking
cons: Building open for over 20 years, some spots getting worn · elevator has had problems
Some bathrooms have a musty smell and towels are sometimes short
Reviews mention mosquitoes at night and fairly thin walls

entries.addr: 23/1 Kilometer 2 Road (right side), Aranyaprathet Subdistrict, Aranyaprathet District, Sa Kaeo
entries.storyHtml: If budget is the starting point and you just need a clean, quiet bed for a night, Chaisuk Bungalow is the stay with the cheapest starting price in this article, around ฿350/night — several single-story bungalows in a garden in the Aranyaprathet area, near the train station and the Khlong Luek checkpoint · The strength is simplicity done well at a very easy price, with real reviews agreeing the rooms are clean, the air conditioning is nicely cold, and the atmosphere is quiet and calm, since these are separate bungalows in a garden and thus more private than rooms in a building, plus free parking right at your door, very handy for anyone driving themselves · Rooms come in several tiers to fit your budget, from the cheapest Economy Double starting at ฿350, up to a roomier, better-equipped Superior Double, and a Large Double/Twin that suits small families or groups of friends, all with air conditioning, a TV, a fridge, and hot water · An honest caveat to know before booking: there's no swimming pool or full hotel-style service here — it's an easy-priced bungalow focused mainly on resting and sleeping, so if you want a pool, look at the pricier in-town hotels instead · The location requires a ride of about 10–15 minutes to the Khlong Luek checkpoint and Rong Kluea Market — it's not a walk — so allow time and sort out transport in advance · And some room types have the bathroom located outside, so if you're particular about an en-suite, pick a type that clearly states it has a private bathroom · Best suited to Poipet border crossers, Rong Kluea Market shoppers, and anyone arriving by train who needs a clean, budget stay near the station
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pick a room type that clearly states it has an en-suite bathroom for convenience, since some types have the bathroom located outside · If you'll cross the border or shop at Rong Kluea Market, allow about 10–15 minutes of ride time and sort out transport in advance
pros: Starting at just around ฿350/night, the cheapest in this article
Clean rooms, nicely cold air conditioning, quiet, calm, separate garden bungalows

Near the train station, good for train arrivals looking for a budget stay
cons: No swimming pool or full hotel-style service
Location requires a ride to the Khlong Luek checkpoint and Rong Kluea Market, not a walk
Some room types have the bathroom located outside

entries.storyHtml: Suan Ko Kae Resort is a small 2-star bungalow resort with about 26 rooms in a suburban zone of Aranyaprathet, especially well suited to self-drivers · The strength real reviews mention is the roomy, clean bungalows with comfortable beds and a quiet, calm setting, plus free parking right by your room, which is very convenient for anyone driving themselves who doesn't want to worry about parking like in the town center · On top of that, the free Wi-Fi works well, there's hot water for tea and coffee in the morning, and the staff are friendly with easy check-in — everything is simple but covers the essentials for a comfortable overnight, starting at around ฿700/night · Rooms come as Standard, a roomier Superior that suits couples, and a Family Room that sleeps several and suits families driving in · An honest caveat that has to be said plainly from the reviews: the building and decor look a bit dated in some spots, and the location is about 19 kilometers from Rong Kluea Market and the Khlong Luek checkpoint, which is considerably farther than the other stays in this set, so without your own car it'll be a hassle, and you should pick an in-town stay closer to the border instead · On top of that, there's no swimming pool, no full breakfast, and no 24-hour front desk, so if you need those, consider an in-town boutique like Tournesol or La Villa instead · Best suited to self-drivers stopping over before crossing the border or coming for business in Aranyaprathet town, who want a quiet, roomy bed at a budget price
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: This is most suited to self-drivers, since parking is right by your room and the location is about 19 km from the market and border · If you don't have your own car, or you want a swimming pool and 24-hour front desk, consider an in-town boutique like Tournesol or La Villa instead

faqTitle: FAQ — Questions travelers often ask about hotels in Aranyaprathet, Sa Kaeo

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best hotel in Aranyaprathet?
faq.a: It depends on your travel style · Measured on score alone, Indochina Hotel is the highest in the article at 8.9, with a large pool, new rooms, and good breakfast · If you're with family and want the kids to have fun, The Velo's Hotel has a BMX Pump Track and a saltwater pool · If you want to stay by the border for an early crossing, At Border Hotel is a walk to the Poipet border · If warm service matters, OB-Oon Resort · And on a tight budget, Chaisuk Bungalow starts at just ฿350

faq.q: ❓ How much do hotels in Aranyaprathet cost?
faq.a: In this article, prices start around ฿350–1,500 per night · On the budget end are Chaisuk Bungalow from ฿350, Station ONE ฿600, At Border ฿680, and Suan Ko Kae ฿700 · Mid-range are My Room by Sermsub ฿800, OB-Oon ฿880, Tournesol ฿1,000, La Villa ฿1,200, and Indochina ฿1,400 · The top of the set is The Velo's Hotel from ฿1,500 (Pool Access rooms up to around ฿2,400) · All prices are approximate starting rates from standard rooms; during festivals and heavy border-crossing periods prices may be higher than usual

faq.q: ❓ Where should I stay if I'm crossing to Poipet at the Khlong Luek checkpoint?
faq.a: If you want to walk straight to the border without calling a ride, At Border Hotel ฿680 is next to Rong Kluea Market and a few steps' walk to the Poipet border, best suited to anyone rushing to cross early · If you want a nicer stay in town, Station ONE ฿600 and My Room by Sermsub ฿800 are in the town center near the border and market · And OB-Oon Resort ฿880 and Chaisuk Bungalow ฿350 are about 10–15 minutes' ride from the border, suiting those with a car

faq.q: ❓ Which hotels in Aranyaprathet have a swimming pool?
faq.a: In this article, the stays with a clear swimming pool are The Velo's Hotel (semi-Olympic saltwater pool + slide), Indochina Hotel (large saltwater pool with attractive landscaping), Tournesol Boutique (saltwater pool, separate kids' pool), and La Villa Boutique (has a swimming pool and a Finnish sauna) · The budget stays like Chaisuk Bungalow, Station ONE, At Border, and Suan Ko Kae have no pool, focusing on value and location instead

faq.q: ❓ Aranyaprathet, no car of my own — how do I get around?
faq.a: Aranyaprathet has no rail system and limited public transport, and Grab is scarce in the area · If you don't have your own car, the convenient way is to take a train or bus to the Aranyaprathet bus terminal/station, then have your hotel arrange transfers or a local songthaew · Town-center stays like Station ONE are a walk to the bus terminal, and My Room by Sermsub has free transfers within a short radius, a big help for those without a car

faq.q: ❓ How far in advance should I book a hotel in Aranyaprathet?
faq.a: Several stays in this article are small (some just about 6–18 rooms), so they fill up fast · During long weekends and festivals when crowds flock to Rong Kluea Market and the border crossing, book 2–4 weeks ahead or more, especially OB-Oon, La Villa, and My Room by Sermsub, which have few rooms · In normal periods, 1–2 weeks is enough · Every platform usually offers Free Cancellation, so we recommend locking in a rate like that first if your plans aren't set, then comparing Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price
